title: fix(plugin-approvals): a request's subject title is served only from fields its reader may read
body:
Fixes #23594
Clause-②: no

A request's subject title (`record_title`) is now served only from fields its reader may be served. The one-tap action-link pages, which have no reader to narrow for, name the record by its id. Function level only, per the card.

## What changed

All in `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals`.

- **One answer per reader, asked once.** `ApprovalService.servedSubjectFields` asks `resolveReadableSnapshotFields` (`payload-redaction.ts`, the #10749 seam: readable, and not masked for this caller) once per subject object of a read, as the reading caller. Both serve-time narrowings of a row read this map:
  - `redactPayloads` redacts the payload snapshot with it, as before (now synchronous, fed the map);
  - `resolveSubjectDisplays` picks the title from the subject record as served to the reader: `redactSnapshot(record, served)`, then the existing `pickTitle`.
  `enrichRows` takes the map as a required argument, so no caller can reach the title without stating the narrowing.
- **What a reader gets.** A display field the reader may not read, or is served masked (#20964), gives no title: the key is absent, the shape the redaction gives that field in the payload. A title-eligible field the reader may read (`name`, `title`, `subject`, `label`) still names the record, which is how the snapshot fallback already picked its title. A reader who may read the display field gets the same title as before. The seam's pass-through (no security service wired, an unresolvable schema, a throwing read projection) passes the title through exactly as it passes the snapshot. Nothing is granted: record access stays with object permissions, sharing and row-level rules (#7497 ruling C).
- **Action-link pages** (`action-link-pages.ts`, `summaryRows`). The "Record" row shows the record id beside the object's label, never the title, on both the confirm and the result page, through both doors (the self-hosted mount and `handleActionPage`).

## The dispatch's mechanism assumptions, measured on `origin/main` `a6d0715535`

1. **Held.** `listRequests` and `loadRequest` already redacted the payload by the caller (`redactPayloads`), then `resolveSubjectDisplays` read the subject under `SYSTEM_CTX` and picked the title from the whole record, once per object, for every reader. The narrowing now sits where the payload's does, with the same answer.
2. **Held already, measured.** The title's snapshot fallback (`pickTitle(r.payload)` in `enrichRows`) reads the payload after `redactPayloads` has redacted it for the reader, so a deleted subject never leaked a withheld snapshot field. Pin (b) is green on the old code and on the new.
3. **Toasts:** every request action's read-back row (`readBackRequest` to `loadRequest`) is enriched under the acting caller's context, so the success copy's `result.request.record_title` token is narrowed by this change. **Action-link pages:** the token chain reads the request with `getRequest(..., SYSTEM_CTX)` (peek) and decides under the system context with the slot's person attached (redeem). Field-level security does not narrow a system context (`plugin-security` returns the full set for `isSystem`), so the page cannot be narrowed for its bearer. Per the dispatch, the title is withheld there, not granted, for every bearer.
4. **Not built; reported.** The subject's own declared API exposure does not gate the payload snapshot: the #10749 header states the seam "does not gate on OBJECT-level access". Gating the title by exposure while the same field ships in the snapshot would be a second rule beside the redaction. 896a4342e6 gated a SECOND object's titles (`payload_display` lookup targets), which no approval routes the reader to. Whether exposure should gate the approval path at all is a separate design question.

## Pins

New `subject-title-reader-fls.integration.test.ts`: the real `ApprovalService` on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (in-memory better-sqlite3), with a field-visibility source standing in for `plugin-security`'s.

- (a) A reader who may not read the display field gets no title on `getRequest` and `listRequests`. The payload is narrowed by the same answer. A display field served masked is withheld the same way.
- (b) The same reader, subject deleted, snapshot carrying the title: no title. Control: the reader who may read it gets the snapshot's title.
- (c) The decision result row, which the toast token reads, carries no title for that reader.
- (d) The action-link confirm and result pages name the record by its id and carry no title, for a restricted bearer and for a reader alike.
- (e) Control: a reader who may read the field gets the title on the single read, the list and the decision result.
- (f) A withheld display field lends nothing: with the display field withheld and another title-eligible field readable, the title is the readable field's value, and the withheld value appears nowhere on the row.
- (g) One rule, asked once: one field-visibility ask per object per read, on the single read and on a multi-row list.

Updated: `action-page-member.integration.test.ts`, the POST parity twin case (a token is single-use, so twins now differ by their record ids alone; byte-equal once that difference is named, and each page equals the renderer's page for its own request). `payload-display-target-exposure.test.ts` and `implicit-reference-target-lookup.test.ts` pass the new required argument (an empty map: no answer for any object). One comment in `approval-requested-notification.integration.test.ts` no longer says the inbox title is unnarrowed.

## Red before, ablations after

- **Before the fix**, the new file on `a6d0715535` plus the pins: 5 failed / 3 passed. The failures were (a) twice, (c), (d) and (f); (b), (e) and (g) were green.
- **Ablation 1**, at commit `67fd2c6bee`, via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` under an EXIT/INT/TERM trap. The served-view line in `resolveSubjectDisplays` was replaced by the old whole-record pick. Predicted: red on (a), (a masked), (c) and (f). Observed: 4 failed / 4 passed, exactly those. Restore proven: blob `daeac5d639c7` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Ablation 2**, same tool. The old `record_title || record_id` row was put back in `summaryRows`. Predicted: red on (d). Observed: 1 failed / 7 passed, that one. Restore proven: blob `4123cfb893a1` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- No `dist` step: every subject is imported from `src` by relative path.

## Tests and gates

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (whole package, at `67fd2c6bee`, before the merge of `origin/main` `8d05456cbe`): Test Files 75 passed (75), Tests 1062 passed (1062), lock VERDICT command-exit 0. The merge brought only `plugin-auth`, `plugin-email`, `AGENTS.md` and a `scripts/pm` file, none in this package or its dependency closure.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` OK (8 files / 324 errors / 27 signatures held). `tsc --listFiles` on `tsconfig.test.json` compiles all five edited or new test files.
- Gates: at `d3ca88e8d3` (the final head), `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 commands. All 67 ran, each exit code captured before any pipe, and all 67 exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` first answered 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (no workspace dist). After a workspace build (75 tasks, exit 0), both answered 0; they are recorded at that measured 0, not as failures. `--ran` reconciliation: 67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN (exit 0). eslint over the 7 changed TS files: exit 0, no findings. The local-only families (`check:dev-prereqs`, `check:skill-frame-freshness`) are not owed: no `packages/spec` build input or frame file is touched. The full farm is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **The toast for a withheld title reads `Approved ""`** (and likewise for the other eight success messages). The action runner's `${result.*}` grammar substitutes an absent path with an empty string and has no fallback operator. This is the same shape any subject with no resolvable title already toasts (920bc12's own acceptance note); this change adds the readers whose title is withheld to it. It leaks nothing, and the inbox's own inline approve and reject copy falls back to the formatted record id. Not fixed here: it needs either a fallback in the runner's token grammar (objectui) or a server-named, always-present display field (a contract addition).
- **The action-link pages withhold the title from every bearer**, a reader who could read it included. They have no session to narrow under. Narrowing them under the slot's person would mean resolving that person's grants outside a request (`resolveUserAuthzGrants`), the per-recipient mechanism the seat declined for the notification body.
- **`nameSubjectRecord`'s inline comment** ("withheld until resolveSubjectDisplays narrows it by each reader's FLS") names a condition this PR meets in the inbox. The notification still has no reader to narrow for, so its title stays withheld. The comment is left untouched, as the dispatch ruled (#23556's remaining half owns it).
- **Not measured here:** a full composition with `plugin-security` resolving a real permission set. The pins hold the seam to the field-visibility contract's answers, as the payload pins do.
- **Read, not measured, not filed (no carrier):** the record-lock refusal in `lifecycle-hooks.ts` (`recordTitleOf`) names the record's title to the writer from the engine's update pre-image. Whether that pre-image is narrowed for the writer's field-level security was not measured.
